title: An Engineering Case Study of the Tarbela T-5 Water Ingress: Assessment of Failure Hypotheses and Lessons from Historical Dam Failures
content: On 9 November 2026, while excavating the second bench of the connecting tunnel, a water-ingress event was reported at the Tarbela 5th Extension Hydropower Project (T-5). Project officials blamed the inflow on the failure of weak rock between the intake pit and the tunnel, while accounts from the Haripur Deputy Commissioner said it was due to a failure of a protective bund and another report cited a falling girder. There is also a different public accounts, with respect to the workforce outcome. The incident is located within a geographical and hydraulic context, the two accounts are compared on a set of common criteria, and three testable hypotheses, resulting from the analysis of the mechanisms, are presented: rock-mass failure, temporary-barrier failure, and a coupled sequence. The comparison is then made to three known failures: Teton Dam (1976), Oroville Spillway (2017), and Vajont landslide (1963). These cases are not considered proof of the T-5 failure mechanism, but rather provide lessons to be transferred for future projects. Project-history context is provided in the separate inquiry on upstream-cofferdam which was held in August 2025. No public records of the initiating cause exist, and a conclusion must involve the inquiry record, site evidence, construction documentation and monitoring data.
